prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Aliases: Medication Order Gateway=Morrowglass; Pharmacy Technician=Copperfield; Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot=Cinderwake; Pharmacy Verification Station=Juniper; Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler=Bluejay; Registered Nurse=Larkspur; Medication Return Kiosk=Tallowmere; Biomedical Engineer=Stonewake. Morrowglass validates/timestamps orders, retains rejections, produces Order Reconciliation Snapshot. Cinderwake reconciles orders/dispenses/cabinets, preserving identifiers/context/authorization/times/dispositions; excludes cancellations, honors corrections, reviews duplicates, retains remainders; holds disagreements, stops affected picks, produces Priority Refill Tote Tag. Copperfield authorizes replenishment with clear queue; clinical restrictions prevail. Clinical Pharmacist produces Dose Exception Review Slip, resolves orders through Morrowglass; release requires authorization. Serious/time-critical exceptions escalate immediately. Medication Safety Officer reviews diversion/repeated-risk/harm and identity/access/patient-risk discrepancies. IT Operations Specialist receives Diversion Review Packet; investigations cannot change clinical disposition. Juniper checks order/product/dose/patient/label; Copperfield checks integrity/lot/expiry/cold-chain. High-risk releases require recorded independent checks; inconclusive/mismatched reviews remain held. Juniper records approval/evidence/disposition, produces Batch Release Note; Copperfield produces Cold Chain Handoff Card; Hospital Courier records custody/produces Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record. East Tube Dispatch Console checks approved routes/interlocks; stale/incomplete/lost-sensor status blocks routing. Pneumatic Tube Network reports status/progress/delivery. Interruptions record location/time; East alerts Copperfield, sends Tube Route Exception Ticket; West Tube Dispatch Console controls authorized routing. Recovery requires refreshed status/approved routing; alternatives require approved custody. North Ward Cabinet Controller uses tote tag/blocks holds; South Ward Cabinet Controller receives release note, checks approved-version mapping/access/classes; Ready for Dispense requires configuration/self-tests. Both record arrivals/destinations/failures. Larkspur checks refrigeration/locks, authenticates/selects active-order medication; authorization precedes unlocking; audit retains user/order/access/time/equipment/disposition. Identity/configuration failures block dispensing. Stonewake correlates operational record/exception ticket with telemetry, assesses service scope, isolates faults using approved diagnostics; records correction/tests/approvals. Faulted/unresponsive/failed-check cabinets remain Out of Service until functional checks/staff approval. Pharmacist withholds medication pending repeated order/product checks. IT uses Cabinet Downtime Notice for controlled incident/equipment/detection-time recording; checks

New part:
S227: The Medication Order Gateway retains pending requests for review rather than treating an interrupted transaction as completed.
S228: The IT Operations Specialist checks whether any transaction was interrupted before the cabinet became unavailable.
S229: The Pharmacy Verification Station is used to confirm that pending medication orders remain valid before they are re-presented.
S230: The Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot is held from supplying medication to a cabinet that has not passed its recovery checks.
S231: The IT Operations Specialist coordinates technical troubleshooting with the Biomedical Engineer when equipment inspection or repair is required.
S232: The Clinical Pharmacist reviews medication orders affected by the outage when clinical validation is needed.
S233: The Registered Nurse uses the established clinical process for urgent medication needs while the cabinet is unavailable.
S234: The Biomedical Engineer reports completed repairs and any equipment limitations to the IT Operations Specialist.
S235: After repair, the IT Operations Specialist verifies communications, status reporting, and cabinet transaction behavior under controlled conditions.
S236: The responsible staff confirm that no unresolved transaction could cause a duplicate or missed dispense.
S237: The cabinet remains Out of Service until required functional checks pass and the responsible staff approve its return to Ready for Dispense.
S238: The West Tube Dispatch Console uses the Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record to verify capsule identity and seal status before closing its dispatch-side handoff checks.
S239: The West Tube Dispatch Console records completion of its handoff checks only after the required dispatch data are consistent.
S240: The Pneumatic Tube Network remains under monitoring while dispatch service is being restored.
S241: The Hospital Courier confirms physical receipt through the established delivery process.
S242: The West Tube Dispatch Console retains the handoff completion status for operational review.
S243: The IT Operations Specialist monitors cabinet and tube service status for recurrence during the recovery period.
S244: Audit records retain timestamps, equipment identifiers, recovery checks, and disposition details to support operational review and investigation.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
